main_text.p: & diu cupidè defiderauerant, tria effe po‐terant documenta, vifus, affectus & cachin‐nus & grandiloquentia. De his ordine, οὶω agendum nobis erit.

1. De vsu. Quicunque oderunt aliquem, vbi aduerfis circumuentum illum esse ani‐maduertunt, truci aspectu & defixis in eum oculis, eundem adspiciunt. Ac tū quo‐que id fit, quod vulgò solet dici: Vultu sæpè læditur pietas. Habent enim & frons & o‐culi & vultus suum quendam sermonem, alias gratum, alias moleftissimum. Huc nō nihil faciunt illa Psalmis verba: Dilatauerūt os suum aduersum me, & dixerunt, Euge, euge vidit oculus nofter, Psal. 35. 21.

Rectè sanè Demosthenes alicubi dixit: Oculi sunt indices morū. Truces & distor‐ti ac flammantes oculi, inuidiæ, odij & ma‐leuolentiæ, quasi quidem testes sunt. Ac, vt alicubi Quintilianus prudenter monet, vitijs noftris in animū per oculos via est. Impudicus enim oculus, impudici cordis est nuncius, teste Augustino. Ita elati ocu‐li, vt & latitudo cordis, superbiæ symbola sunt, Psal. 101. 5.
Ideò propheta nofter Obadias, dehorta‐tur Idumæos à peccato oculorum, velut à signo gaudij, quod improbi perciperent li‐benter aspiciendo calamitates & deporta‐tionem

page.notes: Catchword and signature not visible. Probable misprints or unclear letters are not marked in the text; the Greek word after "De his ordine," is partly illegible on the scan and was copied as the nearest Greek form. Psalm references in the text ("Pfal.35.21", "Pfal.101.5") are as printed and may be read as Psal. 35.21 and Psal. 101.5. The line "Ac tū quo-" ends the paragraph with "& deporta-" continuing to "tionem" on the last line.
